A massive batch of U.S. economic data just came in, and the numbers are showing a very mixed picture.

• Q3 GDP: 4.3% vs. 3.5% expected.
• Previous quarter: 2.2%.
• Jobless claims: 189K vs. 200K expected.
• Personal income: +0.7% vs. +0.4% expected.

The economy is growing much faster than expected, unemployment claims remain low, and Americans are earning more.

2. But inflation is still running too high.

• Annual PCE inflation: 3.8% vs. 3.7% previously.
• Monthly PCE: 0.3%, in line with expectations.
• Core PCE: 0.3%, also in line.

3. There are also signs that parts of the economy are slowing.

• Durable goods orders: +0.2% vs. +0.6% expected.
• Consumer spending: +0.3% vs. +0.4% expected.
• Corporate profit growth: 3.8% vs. 7.7% previously.
• GDP price index: 1.8% vs. 2.3% expected.

So businesses are seeing slower profit growth, and consumers aren't spending as quickly as expected.

But there is some positive news.

Monthly PCE inflation slowed from 0.5% to 0.3%, while the GDP price index came in much cooler than expected.

Oil prices have also fallen sharply this month, which could help reduce inflation in the coming months.

• Dec. 9: Fed interest rate decision
• Dec. 10: November CPI inflation

Entonces, lo involucra con unos mafiosos para ganar más dinero, pero termina baleado, a punto de perder la vida y con su casa quemada.

$SPX | One final shakeout before the next major bullish leg — and potentially a Cycle Top above 10,000? 🚨

My preferred Elliott Wave roadmap suggests a multi-stage bullish continuation with now a complex correction with a fakeout (in form of a expanded flat) but still the sequence and key invalidation levels are crucial.

1. Wave (3) – Potentially Completed

The August high around 7,800 may have marked the end of the lower-degree Wave (3).

2. Wave (4) – Expanded Flat (3-3-5)

(a): Initial decline toward ~7,484
(b): Corrective rebound toward/above ~7,800
(c): Final five-wave decline, potentially completing Wave (4) within 7,250–7,480

3. Wave (5) – Final Push to Complete Higher-Degree Wave III

Following confirmation of Wave (4), a renewed bullish impulse could target:

T1: 8,057 – Initial Fibonacci/technical resistance
T2: 8,473 – Higher extension
T3: 8,782 – Extended bullish target

The upper boundary of the ascending broadening wedge provides additional structural confluence.

4. Higher-Degree Wave IV

A larger corrective phase could follow the completion of Wave III.

5. Higher-Degree Wave V

A final impulsive advance could potentially carry $SPX above 10,000, forming a major Cycle Top — subject to confirmation of the higher-degree wave structure.

Key Validation & Invalidation Levels

~7,800: Wave (b) must exceed the starting high of (a) to qualify as an Expanded Flat.
7,484: Wave (c) must terminate below the (a) low for the Expanded Flat count to remain valid.
7,250: Lower boundary of the preferred Wave (4) target region. A breakdown would require reassessing the correction depth, but is not automatically an Elliott Wave invalidation.
~7,000: Approximate Wave (1) high. A Wave (4) overlap with Wave (1) invalidates the standard impulsive count. The exact Wave (1) high must be verified.
After Wave (4) completes: A break below its confirmed low invalidates the proposed start of an impulsive Wave (5) from that low.

The key distinction: Lower-degree Waves (3)-(4)-(5) complete the larger Wave III. Only afterward would higher-degree Waves IV and V unfold.

Disclaimer: All Fibonacci projections, target zones and timing assumptions are conditional. Their exact values depend on the final termination points of the developing waves and must be recalculated as the structure evolves. The 10,000+ Cycle Top remains a speculative higher-degree scenario, not a confirmed target.
